vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: mails-for-agent
Version: 1.7.2

The skill bundle (SKILL.md) provides an interface for an email automation service specifically designed for 'autonomous service registration' by extracting verification codes (OTPs) via a long-polling API (/api/code). The instructions also include a flow for deleting emails after processing, which facilitates stealthy automated account creation. While these high-risk capabilities are transparently documented and require user-provided credentials, the inherent risk of bypassing registration controls and the potential for automated botting warrants a suspicious classification.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and runtime instructions are coherent with an email/inbox automation capability; nothing requested is disproportionate to that purpose, although there are a couple of small inconsistencies in the docs you should verify before use.

dimensions.detail: Name and description (receive verification codes, send/receive/monitor email, download attachments) align with the declared requirements (MAILS_API_URL, MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN, MAILS_MAILBOX) and the API endpoints the SKILL.md documents. The requested environment variables are exactly what an HTTP-based mailbox worker would need.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are limited to calling the documented API endpoints using the three declared env vars and describe inbox flows (GET /api/inbox, GET /api/code, POST /api/send, DELETE /api/email, etc.). Notable inconsistencies: the doc shows a long-poll example GET /api/code?timeout=60 but Constraints state the code wait timeout max is 55 seconds — this is contradictory and should be clarified. Also SKILL.md version is 1.7.0 while registry lists 1.7.2 (minor doc/version drift).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files (instruction-only). This is lowest-risk from install perspective because nothing is written to disk by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The three required env vars (API URL, auth token, mailbox) are proportional to the documented HTTP API usage. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or config paths are requested. The primary credential being MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN matches the described Authorization header usage.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request system-wide or persistent privileges. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but not combined with any excessive environment access in this skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: talk to a mailbox API and retrieve/send email using the three environment variables. Before installing, verify the MAILS_API_URL points to a trusted provider and that the MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN has only the necessary scope (not broader system-wide credentials). Confirm the mailbox value is the intended address and avoid using this with mailboxes you care about for critical accounts unless you fully trust the service. Ask the publisher to clarify the timeout inconsistency (GET /api/code?timeout=60 vs. documented max 55s) and the SKILL.md/version drift. Be aware the skill can delete messages and send mail on behalf of the mailbox—grant access only if you accept those capabilities.
